questions.title: Work & Time Efficiency Calculation
questions.description: Worker A can finish a software module in 12 days, while Worker B can finish the same module in 18 days. If they work together with Worker C and finish the module in 4 days, in how many days can Worker C alone complete the entire module?
questions.explanation: Total 1 day work of A + B + C = 1/4. Work of A = 1/12, Work of B = 1/18. Therefore, 1 day work of C = 1/4 - (1/12 + 1/18) = 1/4 - (5/36) = (9 - 5)/36 = 4/36 = 1/9. Hence C alone completes the task in 9 days.
hints: Find the combined rate per day: Rate(A) + Rate(B) + Rate(C) = Rate(Total)

questions.title: Logical Deduction & Sequence Pattern
questions.description: Identify the next missing number in the following algorithmic sequence: 4, 18, 48, 100, 180, ?
hints: Try expressing each term as a cube minus square or product of two powers.

questions.title: Python Scoping & Mutable Default Arguments
questions.description:
What will be the exact output of executing the following Python snippet?

```python
def append_to_list(val, my_list=[]):
    my_list.append(val)
    return my_list

print(append_to_list(10))
print(append_to_list(20, []))
print(append_to_list(30))
```
questions.explanation: In Python, default arguments are evaluated once when the function is defined, not each time the function is called. The list `my_list` is shared across invocations that do not pass an explicit second argument. In the 2nd call, a fresh list `[]` was explicitly passed so it did not mutate the default list. The 3rd call reuses the mutated default list `[10]`, resulting in `[10, 30]`.
hints: Default arguments in Python are instantiated at definition time and reused across calls.

questions.title: Java OOPs: Polymorphism & Method Overriding
questions.explanation: In Java, member variables (fields) do not exhibit polymorphism and are resolved at compile-time based on the reference type (`p` is of type `Parent`, so `p.x` accesses `Parent.x = 10`). However, non-private instance methods are dynamically dispatched at runtime based on the actual object instance (`this` is an instance of `Child`, so `p.print()` invokes `Child.print()`, which prints `20`).
hints: Variable binding is determined at compile-time by reference type, whereas virtual method dispatch happens at runtime.

questions.title: JavaScript Event Loop & Microtask Queues
questions.explanation: 1 and 5 are synchronous calls and run immediately. Next, microtasks (Promises) in the microtask queue run before macrotasks: Promise chain prints 3, then 4. Finally, the macrotask (`setTimeout` callback) executes and prints 2.
hints: Synchronous code -> Microtask queue (Promises) -> Macrotask queue (setTimeout).

questions.title: Data Structures: Time Complexity of Linked List Cycle Detection
questions.description: What is the optimal auxiliary space complexity of Floyd’s Cycle-Finding Algorithm (Tortoise and Hare) for detecting a cycle in a singly linked list with N nodes?
questions.explanation: Floyd’s Cycle-Finding algorithm uses two pointers (`slow` moving 1 step and `fast` moving 2 steps). It only stores two memory pointers, requiring O(1) auxiliary constant memory space while traversing in O(N) time.
hints: Unlike a HashSet approach which requires storing visited node references in O(N) space, two-pointer tracking needs no external buffers.

questions.title: Algorithms: Optimal Substructure in Two Sum / Hash Lookup
questions.description: Given an unsorted array of N integers, what is the most optimal average time complexity to find if there exist two elements whose sum equals a target value K?
options: O(N) time using a Hash Map
O(N log N) time using Sorting and Binary Search
questions.correctAnswer: O(N) time using a Hash Map
questions.explanation: By iterating through the array once and storing each seen number in a Hash Map (or Hash Set), we can check in O(1) average time if the complement `K - num` has already been encountered, achieving an optimal O(N) time and O(N) space complexity.
hints: Complement lookup: For each element x, check if (K - x) exists in the table.

questions.title: Operating Systems: Deadlock Necessary Conditions
questions.description: Which of the following is NOT one of the four Coffman conditions necessary for a system deadlock to occur?
questions.explanation: The four necessary Coffman conditions for deadlock are: 1) Mutual Exclusion, 2) Hold and Wait, 3) No Preemption (resources cannot be forcibly taken from processes), and 4) Circular Wait. "Preemptive Resource Allocation" actually prevents deadlocks rather than causing them.
hints: If resources can be preempted, deadlocks can be resolved and broken.

questions.title: DBMS: SQL Normalization & Dependency Preserving
questions.description: A relation R is in Third Normal Form (3NF) if it is in 2NF and:
options: Every non-prime attribute is non-transitively dependent on every candidate key
Every determinant is a candidate key (BCNF condition)
Every non-key attribute is partially dependent on the primary key
questions.correctAnswer: Every non-prime attribute is non-transitively dependent on every candidate key
questions.explanation: 3NF strictly eliminates transitive functional dependencies: for every functional dependency X -> Y, either X is a super key or Y is a prime attribute (part of a candidate key).
hints: 2NF removes partial key dependencies; 3NF removes transitive dependencies.

questions.title: System Design: Caching Strategy Trade-offs
questions.description: In a high-throughput read-heavy web application, which caching strategy writes data directly to the cache and the database simultaneously to guarantee immediate read consistency?
questions.explanation: In Write-Through caching, data is written into the cache and the permanent database store concurrently before the write operation returns success. This ensures the cache is never stale, though it introduces higher write latency compared to Write-Back.
hints: Write-back writes to cache first and async batches to DB; Write-through writes to both synchronously.

companies.name: Google
companies.description: Global tech giant famous for search, cloud, AI, and large-scale distributed systems. Interviews emphasize data structures, algorithmic optimization, and clean architectural design.

hiringRounds.name: Online Coding Assessment
hiringRounds.description: 2-3 algorithmic problems (Graph, DP, Sliding Window, Trees) on a timed platform (90 mins).
tips: Focus on edge cases and optimal O(N) or O(N log N) time complexity.

hiringRounds.name: Technical Interview I (DSA & Coding)
hiringRounds.description: 45-minute live coding session on Google Docs or shared editor solving complex algorithmic challenges.
tips: Think out loud continuously. Clarify assumptions before writing code.

hiringRounds.name: Technical Interview II (Advanced DSA / System Design)
hiringRounds.description: Deep dive into data architecture, scalability, cache management, or complex problem solving.
tips: Discuss trade-offs between space and time. Show willingness to iterate.

hiringRounds.name: Googliness & Leadership (HR)
hiringRounds.description: Assesses cultural fit, navigating ambiguity, collaborative teamwork, and ethical decision making.
tips: Use the STAR framework (Situation, Task, Action, Result) with quantified impacts.

companies.name: Amazon
companies.description: Leader in e-commerce, cloud infrastructure (AWS), and streaming. Interviews rigorously test Amazon Leadership Principles alongside DSA.

hiringRounds.name: Online Assessment (OA1 & OA2)
hiringRounds.description: 2 Coding questions + Work Style Assessment (Leadership Principles behavioral quiz).
tips: Make sure all public & hidden test cases pass.
Align answers strictly with LP values (Customer Obsession, Ownership).

hiringRounds.name: Technical Interview 1
hiringRounds.description: Core DSA coding problem with follow-up scaling questions + 2 LP behavioral questions.
tips: Prepare 2 distinct real-life stories per leadership principle.

hiringRounds.name: Technical Interview 2 & Bar Raiser
hiringRounds.description: In-depth problem solving, Object-Oriented Design (LLD), and Bar Raiser standard evaluation.
tips: Show robust OOP principles (SOLID, encapsulation, clean interfaces).

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.description: Pioneer in enterprise cloud (Azure), operating systems, and developer tooling. Focuses on strong CS fundamentals, OS, OOP, and algorithms.

hiringRounds.name: Online Assessment
hiringRounds.description: 3 coding questions on Codility or Mettle measuring problem solving and speed.
tips: Practice writing bug-free code quickly. Edge cases like empty inputs matter.

hiringRounds.name: Technical Round 1 (DSA & Core CS)
hiringRounds.description: Linked Lists, Binary Trees, Operating System internals, and Memory Management.
tips: Explain OS concepts clearly (Paging, Virtual Memory, Process vs Thread).

hiringRounds.name: Technical Round 2 & Cultural Fit
hiringRounds.description: Advanced algorithms, project architecture discussion, and growth mindset assessment.
tips: Be ready to defend architectural choices made in your college/personal projects.

companies.name: TCS (Tata Consultancy Services)
companies.description: Premier global IT services and consulting enterprise. Evaluates through the National Qualifier Test (TCS NQT) for Ninja and Digital/Prime roles.

hiringRounds.name: TCS NQT (Cognitive & Coding Assessment)
hiringRounds.description: Section 1: Numerical Ability, Reasoning Ability, Verbal Ability (80 mins). Section 2: Advanced Coding (2 problems, 60 mins).
tips: Accuracy in the Cognitive section is mandatory to unlock Digital/Prime cutoffs.

hiringRounds.name: TR + MR + HR (Technical & Managerial)
hiringRounds.description: Combined interview covering Programming basics, OOPs, SQL queries, resume projects, and relocation flexibility.
tips: Revise standard SQL queries (e.g., 2nd highest salary, grouping) and core OOP principles.

companies.name: Infosys
companies.description: Global leader in digital services and consulting. Hiring tracks include Systems Engineer, Specialist Programmer (SP), and Digital Specialist Engineer (DSE).

hiringRounds.name: InfyTQ / HackWithInfy / Campus Assessment
hiringRounds.description: High-speed Aptitude (Mathematical, Logical, Verbal, Pseudocoding) + 3 DSA coding questions for SP/DSE tracks.
tips: Practice tracing nested loops and recursion pseudocodes under tight time limits.

hiringRounds.name: Technical & HR Interview
hiringRounds.description: Questions on final-year project, database design, web stack, data structures, and interpersonal skills.
tips: Highlight hands-on coding experience and practical project problem-solving.

companies.name: Goldman Sachs
companies.description: Leading global financial institution. Known for rigorous math, high-level quantitative aptitude, core CS, and complex algorithmic coding tests.

hiringRounds.name: Aptitude & Coding Assessment (HackerRank)
hiringRounds.description: Numerical Computation, Logical Reasoning, Advanced Mathematics/Probability, CS Core (OS/DBMS), and 2 Hard Coding questions.
tips: Focus heavily on probability, expected value problems, and optimal graph/tree algorithms.

hiringRounds.name: Technical Round 1 & 2
hiringRounds.description: Problem-solving on whiteboards, time complexity analysis, low-level data structures, and math puzzles.
tips: Be prepared for classical math/logic puzzles (e.g. burning ropes, river crossing, 25 horses).
